name: Lockwood-Mathews Mansion

dates.note: The survey says plainly that 'the sources are contradictory and the Lienau drawings at Avery Library are undated', and reasons to a start in spring 1864 or spring 1865. Recorded as the survey leaves it.

refs.title: Lockwood-Mathews Mansion, Elm Park, Veterans' Memorial Park (southeast corner of West Avenue and Butler Street), Norwalk, Fairfield County, Connecticut
refs.note: The data page's own header prints the older four-letter state form, 'HABS No. CONN-265'. The number is recorded here in the Library's normalised two-letter form, as the schema asks, and the header's form is stated here so a reader who opens the PDF is not surprised.
The item id is the path segment of the data PDF actually fetched.

survey.prepared: The data page reproduces material from Ellen W. Kramer, 'The Domestic Architecture of Detlef Lienau, a Conservative Victorian' (PhD dissertation, New York University, 1958), pp. 183-196, and a printed advertisement of the house dated 1874 in the files of the Norwalk City Planning Commission.

quotes.text: The mansard roofs, dormer windov/s placed Immediately above the cornice line, the emphasis upon corner quoining, the tall chimneys decorated with lienau's favorite bull's eye panels (replaced in the executed design by banded chimneys), the effort to make a balanced composition in spite of unavoidable asymmetries— these are all obviously French in origin.
quotes.page: HABS No. CONN-265 (Page 9) as the data page prints it; the running header 'wcmooD-ymimtis MMSION, ELM PIRK COMNJ HABS No. GONN-265 (Page 9)' follows the span, heavily OCR-corrupted

quotes.text: One should note that none of these plans, vfith the exception of Hobbs' project, an ambitious $150,000 scheme, even remotely approached the scale of the Lockwood rotunda, whose dimensions (32 x 38 feet) exactly corresponded to those of Palladio's Villa Capra (35 x 35 feet).
quotes.page: HABS No. CONN-265, Part II supplemental material; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: It contains stalls for eight horses, carriage and harness rooms, granary and hay loft, and sleeping-room for coachman. It is all fitted up in best manner in hard wood. The farm stable and gardener's cottage in one building, 35 feet by 56 feet, is of wood, two stories, with cow-house underneath. The shop, two story, 24 feet by 30 feet, is built of granite. The farm cottage is built of wood, 26 feet by 36 feet, two story, with cellar under whole building. The ice- house, 30 feet by 45 feet, is of wood.
quotes.page: HABS No. CONN-265, Part II.A, quoting the 1874 printed advertisement; no page marker legible in the extract span

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. Read the second quote before quoting it: the survey says a 32 x 38 ft rotunda 'exactly corresponded' to a 35 x 35 ft one, which is false on its own two figures -- a survey is a source and not an oracle, and the arithmetic in it can be wrong while the measurements are right. Kept as printed. The dependency dimensions are the more useful half for this corpus: the 1874 advertisement gives a whole estate's outbuildings in feet, which is the sort of figure the parti layer has nothing of.
